clinician.final_diagnosis: Pott's puffy tumor (PPT) - frontal bone osteomyelitis with epidural and periosteal abscess secondary to frontal sinusitis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A previously healthy 9-year-old boy presented with a 24-day progressive illness characterized by initial headache that worsened at approximately day 10 with fever. He was treated with penicillin for 7 days but relapsed 4 days after completion with increased frontal swelling, right periorbital pain, and fever up to 40°C. On admission to otorhinolaryngology (day 24), physical examination revealed localized swelling and tenderness on the right forehead from eyebrows to nasal bridge, without fluctuance, redness, or skin softness. Neurological examination was normal. Imaging studies (MRI and CT) confirmed left-sided maxillary, ethmoidal, and frontal sinusitis with frontal bone osteomyelitis, epidural and periosteal abscess with capsular enhancement, and partial superior sagittal sinus obstruction with reactive phlebitis. CT also showed frontal bone erosion internally on the right side. Neurosurgery consultation found no indication for surgical intervention due to absence of neurological deficits and patient's clinical well-being. The patient was treated with intravenous antibiotics for 6 weeks total (1 week hospitalization followed by outpatient continuation with frequent consultations). At 2-month follow-up, the patient achieved complete clinical and radiological remission.
